To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Molecular dynamics simulations have demonstrated that the phase separation in electrolyte mixtures depends on the type of ionic liquid and salt anion.

the molecular dynamics simulations of electrolytes containing ionic liquids and oligoglyme as a solvent for Li(+) have revealed that the phase behavior and the coordination of Li(+) to oligoglyme depend on the ionic liquid used, and that the differences in the coordination of Li(+)-oligoglyme can be explained by the binding energies of the Li(+)-oligo-glyme complexes in solution, which have been calculated using an explicit solvent model.

molecular dynamics simulations can be successfully used to study the structure and dynamics of ternary electrolytes based on ionic liquids and glyme solvents, and that different types of phase separation and Li(+)-coordination can be observed in these electrolytes depending on the ionic liquid/salt anions used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the properties of electrolytes based on ionic liquids and glymes.
the development and application of a new class of electrolytes based on oligoglymes and ionic liquids for lithium-ion batteries.
the development of new electrolyte systems with improved properties, which can be used for the development of new batteries and other energy storage systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of molecular dynamics simulations with explicit or implicit solvent models can give valuable insight into properties and behavior of electrolyte systems.
the implicit solvent models should not be applied to the systems with ionic liquids and the explicit solvent models are required to describe such systems.
the explicit solvent model is more reliable for studying Li(+) coordination in ionic liquids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the explicit solvent approach is necessary for the description of Li(+)-solvent coordination in the presence of ionic liquids.

the explicit model is more reliable in predicting the phase separation of the ternary electrolyte system and the Li(+)-coordination, while the implicit model is more reliable when predicting the binding energies of the complexes.
the choice of an implicit solvent model for the electrolyte is not recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the explicit solvent model can successfully reproduce the structural properties of electrolytes based on ionic liquids and that the binding energies of the Li(+)-glymes complexes are the key factors determining the phase separation and Li(+)-coordination properties in ternary electrolytes.
the choice of ionic liquid and salt anion has a profound effect on the phase behavior and Li(+)-coordination in oligoglyme-based electrolytes.
the choice of the anion in the IL plays a key role in the phase behavior and the Li(+)-glymes association in the electrolyte.
